title: Coding-style findings ledger event (v1)
description: One JSON object per line of a repo-local, append-only, gitignored `.style-findings.jsonl` (main-worktree root). Three event kinds share the file: `finding` (a style violation was seen), `outcome` (what became of it), `gate_pass` (the style gate passed over these files). Current state of a finding = fold of its events in file order: a finding is open until an `outcome` for its id appears; a later `finding` with the same id after an outcome re-opens it (gate source only; l1/l2 re-adds are ignored). Rule clauses (`rule_id`) reference ~/Desktop/colar-agents/CODING-STYLE.md: P0E.n exceptions, P0F.n fallback, P1.n-P3.n, R.n; ruff codes without a clause are `ruff:<CODE>`; the gate's own non-ruff codes without a clause are `gate:<CODE>`. IDs: l1/l2 -> `<repo>:<source>:<run_id>:<display_id>`; gate -> `<repo>:gate:<sha1(file|rule_code|whitespace-stripped line text)[:12]>` so repeated blocks of the same issue fold to one (gate rows carry run_id `gate` and display_id equal to the 12-hex hash). `ts` is local time without timezone (same as .gate-skips.jsonl). Gate-source `sha` is HEAD at commit time, i.e. the parent of the blocked commit (`none` on an unborn branch). ReportFindings status mapping when grading writes outcomes: fixed -> fixed, skipped -> dismissed, no_change_needed -> false_positive. Report-only gate codes (INFO_CODES such as NAME) are not recorded in phase 1.

rule_code.description: What the detector called it: ruff code, gate code (NOQA/DEPTH/USE_PREFIX/SYNTAX) or, for reviewer findings, the clause id.

snippet.description: Optional code context captured when the finding was recorded.
